scenarios.name: winter_reheat_normal
scenarios.description: Reheat doing its job in cold weather: the valve is 60% open at 5 degC outdoors. The heating conjunct is satisfied and the weather conjunct is not, so nothing is reported.

scenarios.name: warm_weather_reheat_active
scenarios.description: The fault: 45% reheat at 26 degC outdoors. Both conjuncts hold from the first tick and the alarm lands at exactly alarm_delay.

scenarios.name: warm_weather_valve_closed
scenarios.description: The reheat conjunct blocking on its own: 26 degC outdoors with the reheat valve shut. Warm weather is not a fault; reheat during warm weather is.

scenarios.name: cold_weather_reheat_wide_open
scenarios.description: The weather conjunct blocking on its own: the valve is 100% open at -5 degC. This is the zone working, and the mirror of warm_weather_valve_closed.

scenarios.name: reheat_exactly_at_the_threshold
scenarios.description: Boundary: the valve sits on exactly reheat_active_threshold (10.0%) in warm weather. Reals.GreaterThreshold is strict and CDL Reals has no GreaterEqual, so exactly on the line reads as closed and the rule stays silent.

scenarios.name: reheat_just_above_the_threshold
scenarios.description: The same line from above: 10.1% of valve travel at 26 degC alarms at 1800 s. Leakage past a shut valve is not this rule's business, and 10% is where the reference draws that line.

scenarios.name: oat_exactly_at_the_lockout
scenarios.description: Boundary on the weather side: OAT sits on exactly zone_heating_lockout_temp (21.0 degC) with the valve at 45%. Strict again, so 21.0 is not yet warm weather.

scenarios.name: oat_just_above_the_lockout
scenarios.description: The same line from above: 21.1 degC alarms at 1800 s.

scenarios.name: morning_warmup_into_a_hot_afternoon
scenarios.description: The realistic trace: the zone is reheating at 18 degC outdoors and the weather crosses the lockout at 600 s. The timer starts on that crossing, not at t=0, so the alarm lands at 2400 s.

scenarios.name: valve_closes_on_the_maturity_tick
scenarios.description: The delay edge from below: the valve shuts at exactly 1800 s. TrueDelay asserts at T + delayTime and drops a falling edge with no lag, so the two land on the same tick and the fault is never reported.

scenarios.name: valve_closes_one_tick_later
scenarios.description: The same edge from above: the valve shuts one tick after maturity, leaving exactly one tick of alarm at 1800 s. The realized test is 'both conditions held for strictly more than alarm_delay' at tick resolution.

scenarios.name: cloud_cover_restarts_the_clock
scenarios.description: Sustained means continuous. OAT drops back under the lockout for ten minutes at 900 s, which discards the elapsed time rather than pausing it, and the alarm lands a full 1800 s after the second crossing at 1500 s.

scenarios.name: lockout_programmed_after_the_alarm
scenarios.description: Recovery: the alarm asserts at 1800 s, someone adds the OAT lockout to the zone sequence at 3600 s and the valve drives shut. The fault clears on that tick — TrueDelay delays the rising edge only.
